statement.p:
How many integer solutions are there to the equation x + y + z = 11 for which
x\text{,} y\text{,} and z are all positive?
x\text{,} y\text{,} and z are all non-negative?
x\text{,} y\text{,} and z are all greater than or equal to -3\text{.}

li.p: {10 \choose 8} solutions. After each variable gets 1 stone for free, we are left with 8 stones and 2 sticks.
{13 \choose 11} solutions. We have 11 stones and 2 sticks.

{22 \choose 2} solutions. This problem is equivalent to finding the number of solutions to x' + y' + z' = 20 where x'\text{,} y', and z' are non-negative. (In fact, we really just do a substitution. Let x = x'- 3\text{,} y = y' - 3 and z = z' - 3).
